_doc: Point-in-time retrospective. Every input was public on as_of; see sources. Hindsight lives only in outcome.json.
methodology: house v2 (EPP-distance adjustment), 6-section format; retro method r2: scenario inputs derived from dated facts by frozen rules (retro/README.md); revenue, net-to-gross, expense, receivables and operating-margin signals with Visa's rule-T thresholds

pit_profile.why: 'Visa is a global payments technology company that facilitates secure, reliable and efficient global commerce and money movement.' 'We face intense competition in our industry.'; no 10-K calls the business cyclical (since the FY2020 10-K none carries the earlier sentence on economic conditions and consumer spending), so the kind is DURABLE; GENAI (live from 2022-11-30) is out of scope: its registered scope names no payments network, and the 10-K's competition words on it concern Visa's value-added services ('The integration of technology like GenAI can create new and better offerings that compete with our value-added services, such as strengthened risk monitoring and managing digital identification.'), not the network; the 10-K adds that stablecoins could disrupt payment networks ('The enactment of the U.S. GENIUS Act in July 2025 and the EU's crypto-asset framework, along with emerging regulatory frameworks in other countries, provide increasing regulatory certainty for stablecoins, which could disrupt existing payment networks, particularly in cross-border, B2B, and currency-unstable markets.'), the company's own reading; CRYPTO is live (from 2020-10-21) and its scope names payments networks: the 10-K's words put it on the watch list, company-acknowledged, with no dated evidence that the market prices it for Visa

theme_watch.reason: Live: Visa's own FY2026 10-K says 'The global payments industry is undergoing significant and rapid technological change, including developments in mobile and other proximity and in-app payment technologies, AI and agentic commerce, machine payments, tokenization, cryptocurrencies, stablecoins, tokenized deposits, distributed ledger and blockchain technologies, cloud-based encryption and authorization, and new digital identity and authentication technologies.' It names a crypto offering of its own: 'In the applications domain, we launched the Visa Stablecoin Platform for stablecoin minting, movement, and management, and we support stablecoin settlement capabilities and stablecoin-linked card programs that help connect digital assets to everyday commerce.' The stock trades at 34.3x FY27E — a premium. Re-file as DISRUPTION_EXPOSED (CRYPTO) only if dated evidence shows the market pricing crypto disintermediation of Visa's network specifically.

classification.quality_note: 'Visa is a global payments technology company that facilitates secure, reliable and efficient global commerce and money movement.' 'We face intense competition in our industry.'; no 10-K calls the business cyclical (since the FY2020 10-K none carries the earlier sentence on economic conditions and consumer spending), so the kind is DURABLE; GENAI (live from 2022-11-30) is out of scope: its registered scope names no payments network, and the 10-K's competition words on it concern Visa's value-added services ('The integration of technology like GenAI can create new and better offerings that compete with our value-added services, such as strengthened risk monitoring and managing digital identification.'), not the network; the 10-K adds that stablecoins could disrupt payment networks ('The enactment of the U.S. GENIUS Act in July 2025 and the EU's crypto-asset framework, along with emerging regulatory frameworks in other countries, provide increasing regulatory certainty for stablecoins, which could disrupt existing payment networks, particularly in cross-border, B2B, and currency-unstable markets.'), the company's own reading; CRYPTO is live (from 2020-10-21) and its scope names payments networks: the 10-K's words put it on the watch list, company-acknowledged, with no dated evidence that the market prices it for Visa. durable franchise (obsolescence risk 2/5); price rich; Ratio B 1.36x; +49% to EPP floor; model-vs-market gap -1.24; conservative 2yr +11%.

BEAR.desc: EPS -10.1%/yr (worst year FY17-FY26, capped at 0%); P/E to its 10th pct

BASE.desc: EPS +15.8%/yr (Q4 revenue YoY + margin + buyback); P/E at its 10-yr median

BULL.desc: EPS +15.8%/yr (FY17-FY26 CAGR, at least BASE); P/E holds its 75th pct

XBULL.desc: EPS +25.0%/yr (best 2-yr run FY17-FY26, at least BULL); P/E at its 90th pct

summary: V (retrospective, 2026-11-06) ◐ WATCHLIST — Ratio B 1.36x (40.9% downside to Bear $249.75 / +30.1% upside to Bull $549.78) | Adj composite 1.64 vs market 2.88: gap -1.24 [OVERVALUED] | +49% above the EPP floor $283.36 (23x FY27E $12.32) | Conservative 2-yr case: +10.9% total (+5.5%/yr) | At 34.3x FY27E the 15% hurdle price $558.95 sits above the BULL case; revenue +13.2% YoY in Q4 FY26, forward revenues +13.2% (Q4 FY26 revenue growth (no FY27 revenue range)); crypto is live and company-acknowledged; no dated evidence ties the multiple to it.
